_readme: Pack counts for current English sealed products, for a 'how many packs is in
this thing?' guide page. RESEARCH OUTPUT ONLY. Nothing here is built yet.
THE RULE: every number carries the source it was read from and the date it
was read. If a field is null, it was NOT sourced and must not be printed.
Look at `sources[].supports` to see which fields each source backs.
NO PULL RATES, NO ODDS, EVER. Nothing in this file states or implies how
likely any card is. Pack counts are printed on the packaging and in official
product listings, so they are verifiable. Odds are not, and are forbidden
sourceTier: 1 = pokemon.com / Pokemon Center / official press
3 = major retailer listing (Target, Walmart, GameStop, Costco)
`id` matches shared/taxonomy.mjs PRODUCT_TYPES so the guide can link to the
existing /openings/<id>.html pages. `id: null` means the site has no tag for

notes.note: 10 cards plus 1 Basic Energy plus a Pokemon TCG Live code card. Sourced on pokemon.com product showcases and on Pokemon Center product pages for Mega Evolution and Scarlet & Violet expansions. The 11-to-10 change happened before the Scarlet & Violet era and was NOT sourced in this pass, so do not state when or why it changed.

notes.topic: 30th Celebration packs are a different size
notes.note: A 30th Celebration booster pack holds 5 foil cards plus 1 foil Basic Energy plus a code card, not 10 cards. Any price-per-card maths on the guide page must exclude 30th Celebration or handle it separately. Pack COUNTS for 30th Celebration products (9 in the ETB, 11 in the Pokemon Center ETB, 6 in the bundle, 4 in the ex Box) are unchanged.

notes.topic: No manufacturer MSRP was found anywhere
notes.note: The Pokemon Company does not publish MSRP on pokemon.com product pages. Every price in this file is either a Pokemon Center store price or a retailer's listed price, and each is labelled with `isMsrp: false` and the retailer it came from. If the guide page wants an MSRP column, it cannot be filled from these sources and should be left out.

GameStop's Chaos Rising Three-Booster Blister lists three packs, one foil promo card and one coin. Target's listing for the same product lists only '3 Booster Packs' and '10 Cards Per Pack' with no promo or coin in its Highlights. Both are recorded on the blister entry. The likeliest reading is that Target's list is incomplete rather than the product differing, but that is inference, so the page should either state both or state only the pack count.

notes.topic: Sources disagreed in presentation: 30th Celebration UPC
notes.note: A search-result summary described the 30th Celebration UPC as '30 booster packs including a special pack'. The pokemon.com page itemises them as two separate lines: 29 standard packs and 1 Classic Collection pack. Same total, different framing. The page should use the itemised version, because the Classic Collection pack is a different product from the other 29.

notes.topic: Trap: standard ETB and Pokemon Center ETB cost the same
notes.note: Target lists the standard Pitch Black ETB at $59.99 and Pokemon Center lists its own 11-pack version at $59.99. If both hold, the Pokemon Center box is two packs and one promo card better at the same money. This is exactly the kind of comparison the page is for, but it rests on two different sellers' prices on one date, so date it and do not present it as a permanent fact.

notes.topic: Trap: the site's ex-premium tag covers two different sizes
notes.note: taxonomy.mjs deliberately folds 'ex Box' into `ex-premium` (the comment there records that all 24 auto-tagged ex-box videos were hand-corrected to ex-premium anyway). But an ex Premium Collection has 8 packs and an ex Box has 4. Both entries are in this file under the same id. The guide page must split them by NAME even though they share a tag, or it will publish a wrong number for half the products on that openings page.

notes.topic: Trap: the tin tag spans 2, 3, 4 and 5 packs
notes.note: The `tin` pattern is a bare \btin\b, so Mini Tins (2 packs), Stacking Tins (3), current standard tins (4) and 2025 standard tins (5) all land on /openings/tin.html. Poke Ball Tins have their own id and 3 packs. A single 'tins have N packs' row would be wrong for most of them.

notes.topic: Products with no product id on this site
notes.note: Build & Battle Box, Battle Deck, Holiday Calendar, Trick or Trade, Collector Chest and Surprise Box have no matching entry in PRODUCT_TYPES. Trick or Trade and any 'Booster Bundle'-named oddity will fall into `bundle` by pattern, and Surprise Box and Collector Chest match nothing at all. If the guide page links every row to an openings page, these rows have nowhere to point.

notes.topic: Openings pages that do not exist yet
notes.note: public/openings/ has pages for blister, bundle, chinese-pack, collection-box, etb, ex-premium, japanese-pack, knock-out, korean-pack, poke-ball-tin, single-pack, tin and upc. There is NO page for spc, ex-special or booster-box, all three of which are in scope for this guide. Those rows cannot link anywhere until the pages exist.

Cards per pack for Ultra-Premium, Super-Premium, ex Premium, ex Box, ex Special, tins and Knock Out. Those products carry mixed-expansion packs and no official page states a per-pack card count for them, so the field is null rather than assumed to be 10. Prices for UPC, SPC, ex Premium, ex Box, ex Special, standard tin, Mini Tin, Knock Out, collection boxes, Build & Battle Box, Battle Deck, Holiday Calendar and Trick or Trade are also unsourced and left null.

pokemon.com, pokemoncenter.com, target.com and gamestop.com all return 403 or a bot-detection interstitial to a plain fetch. Everything here was read through a real browser session. If a later pass gets an 'access interrupted' page, that is the block, not a missing product.

Deliberately absent. No pull rate, hit rate, odds, 'chance of', or god-pack figure appears anywhere in this file, and none should be derived from the pack counts in it. Pack counts are printed on packaging; odds are not published by The Pokemon Company and are forbidden on this site.
